# nel-course — one Markdown source, three outputs.
#
# Everything is built by pandoc from `sections/*.prose.md`. There is no engine
# and no generator: the file list is a shell glob, so the numeric prefixes on the
# section filenames ARE the document order. Add a section by adding a numbered
# pair; nothing needs to be registered anywhere.
#
# CI runs these same recipes (see .github/workflows/pages.yml), so there is one
# definition of how each output is built and no second copy to drift.

outdir := "output"
site   := "_site"
pandoc := "pandoc"
engine := "xelatex"

# `open` is macOS. On Linux:  just open=xdg-open view-doc
open   := "open"

# Shared across all three outputs.
common := "--metadata-file=metadata.yaml --resource-path=.:figures --citeproc --bibliography=references.bib"

# Print available recipes (default).
default:
    @just --list

# Build all three outputs.
build: doc slides site

# --- Document ---------------------------------------------------------------

# output/document.pdf — the long-form read.
doc:
    mkdir -p {{outdir}}
    {{pandoc}} sections/*.prose.md {{common}} \
        --pdf-engine={{engine}} \
        --toc --toc-depth=2 --number-sections \
        -V documentclass=article -V fontsize=11pt -V geometry:margin=1in \
        -o {{outdir}}/document.pdf

# --- Presentation -----------------------------------------------------------

# output/slides.pdf — every `##` heading becomes one slide.
slides:
    mkdir -p {{outdir}}
    {{pandoc}} sections/*.prose.md {{common}} \
        --pdf-engine={{engine}} \
        -t beamer --slide-level=2 \
        -o {{outdir}}/slides.pdf

# Overflowing slides are not a build problem to work around. They are the
# clearest signal you have that a `##` unit is carrying more than one idea, and
# the `visual` reviewer is briefed to report them as writing findings. Fix the
# prose, not the font size.
#
# Nothing here checks for you: pandoc hides the TeX log unless the build fails.
# Look at the deck, or ask the agent to.

# --- Website ----------------------------------------------------------------

# The page links to both PDFs, so this depends on them; without that, a local
# preview has two dead links that only show up after deploying.

# _site/ — one page, sidebar table of contents, both PDFs linked.
site: doc slides
    mkdir -p {{site}}
    {{pandoc}} sections/*.prose.md {{common}} \
        --standalone --toc --toc-depth=2 \
        --template=site/template.html \
        --css=style.css \
        -o {{site}}/index.html
    cp site/style.css {{site}}/
    cp {{outdir}}/document.pdf {{outdir}}/slides.pdf {{site}}/
    mkdir -p {{site}}/figures
    cp -R figures/. {{site}}/figures/
    rm -f {{site}}/figures/README.md

# Serve the site locally at http://localhost:8000.
serve: site
    python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory {{site}}

# --- Viewing ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Open the document PDF.
view-doc: doc
    {{open}} {{outdir}}/document.pdf

# Open the presentation PDF.
view-slides: slides
    {{open}} {{outdir}}/slides.pdf

# --- Publishing -------------------------------------------------------------

# Builds in CI from whatever is on `main` — so commit and push first.
# Requires `gh auth login`, and Pages set to "GitHub Actions" in the
# repository settings.

# Publish the site and both PDFs to GitHub Pages, on demand.
deploy:
    gh workflow run pages.yml
    @echo "Deploy started. Watch it with:  gh run watch"

# --- Housekeeping -----------------------------------------------------------

# Remove all build outputs.
clean:
    rm -rf {{outdir}} {{site}}

1	# nel-course
2	
3	A template for **evolving a document by critique**: one artifact, one Markdown
4	source, three outputs, improved one round at a time by a panel of independent
5	reviewers whose findings are reconciled into a single ranked docket.
6	
7	Clone it, replace the content in `sections/`, and run `/round`.
8	
9	> **[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) is the method.** How a round works, why the reviewers
10	> are independent, what the two registers of a section are for, and the
11	> guardrails — all of it lives there, in one file. This README only covers
12	> getting the toolchain running and starting a project.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## What you get
17	
18	```
19	sections/           the source — one pair of files per section
20	personas/           the reviewer panel, plus the aggregator
21	rounds/             committed critique history: one folder per round
22	site/               the website's template and stylesheet
23	figures/            figures, referenced from the prose
24	topic.md            the proposal — what this tutorial is and promises
25	metadata.yaml       title, authors, and the declared audience
26	justfile            every build recipe
27	```
28	
29	| | Command | Output |
30	| --- | --- | --- |
31	| Document | `just doc` | `output/document.pdf` |
32	| Presentation | `just slides` | `output/slides.pdf` |
33	| Website | `just site` | `_site/index.html` |
34	
35	`just build` makes all three. `just serve` previews the site locally.
36	
37	## Setup
38	
39	Install the toolchain. On macOS:
40	
41	```
42	brew install pandoc just librsvg
43	brew install --cask mactex-no-gui
44	```
45	
46	On Debian or Ubuntu:
47	
48	```
49	sudo apt-get install -y pandoc just texlive-xetex texlive-latex-extra \
50	                        texlive-fonts-recommended librsvg2-bin
51	```
52	
53	Then confirm it works before changing anything:
54	
55	```
56	just build
57	```
58	
59	The placeholder content renders, so a failure here is a toolchain problem, not
60	your writing.
61	
62	## Start your project
63	
64	1. **Say what you are doing.** Fill in [topic.md](topic.md) — the proposal: what
65	   the topic is, why it belongs in this course, what the reader will be able to
66	   do afterwards, and what is out of scope. Every reviewer reads it, and the
67	   panel judges the tutorial against it.
68	2. **Declare your reader.** Edit [metadata.yaml](metadata.yaml) — the title, the
69	   authors, and especially `audience`. The pedagogy reviewer judges the document
70	   against whatever you write there, so a vague audience buys you a vague review.
71	3. **Write.** Replace the placeholders in `sections/`. Each section is a pair:
72	   `<name>.prose.md` ships, `<name>.concepts.md` holds the spine behind it.
73	   Section order is the numeric filename prefix — add a section by adding a
74	   numbered pair.
75	4. **Check it renders.** `just build`.
76	5. **Run a round.** `/round` in Claude Code. It produces a ranked docket at
77	   `rounds/round-NNN/SYNTHESIS.md` and stops; you decide what to act on.
78	
79	## Publishing
80	
81	The site deploys to GitHub Pages on demand — never automatically on push.
82	
83	One-time, in the repository settings: **Settings -> Pages -> Source: GitHub
84	Actions**. Then:
85	
86	```
87	git push
88	just deploy
89	```
90	
91	CI installs the toolchain and runs `just build`, so it publishes exactly what
92	`just serve` showed you. Nothing generated is stored in git.
93	
94	## Derived from
95	
96	The `nel-operator` engine, reduced to its teaching core. The section-pair
97	convention, the reviewer-panel critic, and the never-reverted single manuscript
98	come from there; the compile and metrics gates, the archive, the scaffolder, and
99	the unattended loop deliberately do not.

The "Examples" section is in place between Content and Conclusion, and `just build` passes from a clean state, producing all three outputs.

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `sections/04-examples.prose.md` | New. Three `##` units: "A complete example", "A contrasting example", "Adapting the examples" |

| `topic.md` | `04-conclusion` → `05-conclusion`; "four sections" → "five sections", with a mention of `04-examples` |

- **Order:** the site's headings run Context, Motivation, Content, Examples, Conclusion.
- **Slides:** I rendered the three new slides and none overflow.

- **Placeholder content, not real examples.** The rest of the project is still the unfilled template, so the new section matches it: guidance blockquotes plus "Replace this paragraph."
- **How Examples differs from Content.** Content already has two walkthroughs, so I framed Examples as whole end-to-end cases, with Content's cases being cut down to teach one thing at a time.
- **Renamed with `git mv`.** The two renames are staged so history follows the files. Nothing is committed.
- **Edited `CLAUDE.md` and `topic.md`.** Both named the old numbering and would otherwise have been wrong.

The page count says this was already happening in the four original sections. I left it alone since it's outside this request; the likely cause is the HTML comment between the `#` and the first `##`, but I didn't confirm that.
